bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Sets 500 MW Rooftop Solar Target for Government Buildings by 2029–30 - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Sets 500 MW Rooftop Solar Target for Government Buildings by 2029–30 17 Oct 2026 1 min read Why in News? The Bihar Renewable Energy Development Agency (BREDA) has set a target of installing 500 MW of rooftop solar capacity on government buildings by 2029–30 . Key Points Implementing Agency: Bihar Renewable Energy Development Agency (BREDA) will oversee the installation of grid-connected rooftop solar power plants on government buildings across Bihar. Target: The initiative aims to achieve 500 MW of rooftop solar capacity by 2029–30 . Associated Campaign: The project is being implemented under Phase 3 of the Jal-Jeevan-Hariyali campaign . Implementation Model: Solar projects will be implemented through the Renewable Energy Service Company (RESCO) model . Building Identification: Government departments have been asked to submit lists of buildings under their jurisdiction for assessing their suitability for rooftop solar installations. Power Purchase Agreement: The meeting discussed the draft Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) and the roles and responsibilities of BREDA, government departments and solar developers. national_raw_news.content: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has written letters to the Punjab government seeking detailed reports on two killings and the suicide of a man, amid allegations linked to narcotics and concerns over their potential law-and-order implications in the state. Sources say that the ministry has written three separate letters to the state government in this regard. In one of the letters, the Ministry sought a factual report from the Punjab government on the killing of an activist who was reportedly campaigning against the rampant sale and abuse of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in Punjab. MHA has asked the Punjab government to provide details of the incident and the steps taken in the case. The MHA also sought an update on the action taken by the Punjab government on the Union Home Minister’s Vision Document on Narcotics Control 2026-2029, which was shared with the Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on 10th August this year. Meanwhile, in another letter, the Home Affairs Ministry sought a detailed report on the attack on three individuals in the Mari Panwan village of the Gurdaspur district. The letter noted allegations that the attack was linked to narcotic drugs and asked the state government to share a detailed report in view of the potential law-and-order implications. MHA has also asked the Punjab government to submit a detailed report on the suicide of the father of a youth struggling with substance dependence. It is alleged that the person was subjected to systematic harassment and pressure by the local village Panchayat, which drove him to take his own life.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 185 Centre makes Aadhaar authentication mandatory for Children Scheme of PM CARES
national_raw_news.content: The Centre has made Aadhaar authentication or proof of possession of an Aadhaar number necessary to avail of scholarship benefits under the PM CARES for Children Scheme. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has issued a notification in this regard. It said that beneficiaries of the Special Scholarship Scheme under PM CARES for Children, which provides assistance for continuing education from Class 1st to 12th, will be required to undergo Aadhaar authentication or furnish proof of possession of an Aadhaar number. The notification stated that no child will be denied assistance for failure to authenticate Aadhaar or for not having been assigned an Aadhaar number. In such cases, the benefit will be provided after verifying the child’s identity and establishing the relationship with the parent or legal guardian through the documents specified in the notification. Our correspondent has the details. The notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment provides separate document requirements for beneficiaries below 18 years of age and those aged 18 years or above who have not been assigned an Aadhaar number. Children below 18 years of age can establish their identity by submitting an enrolment acknowledgement containing the Enrolment ID and a document establishing their age, such as a birth certificate, Indian passport or a Class 10th or Class 12th certificate or marks statement issued by a recognised school education board. For beneficiaries aged 18 or above, the notification lists documents such as an Election Commission-issued voter identity card, driving license, Indian passport, and ration card, along with other specified identity documents. The notification also provides for alternative authentication methods, including biometric or one-time password-based verification, wherever feasible, if Aadhaar authentication fails.
